conflict_topics: seat reservation / who may sit at the occupied table
use of a tissue packet as an informal reservation marker
priority for the next available seat when Agent C finishes
time-sensitive need to sit because of hot meals
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers use concise, realistic reasons (sat first; bowl is hot; meal will go cold; tissue as reserve).

Several lines are repeated verbatim across rounds (Agent A repeatedly: 'I left the tissue to reserve this seat'; Agent D repeatedly: 'I'll take the seat when Agent C's finished'), producing moderate repetition.
No environmental actions (moving, leaving) are reported; interactions remain speech-only and consistent with the setting.
Some role confusion/ambiguity about which exact seat D intends (B's or C's) slightly reduces clarity.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A withdrew their claim and conceded the contested arrangement. Evidence: Turn 18 — Agent A: 'Fine. Take the seat.' Turn 22 — Agent D: 'Okay — I'll take it when Agent C's done.' Agent A adjusted by giving up their reservation claim; Agent D's stated sequence (taking the seat after C finishes) stands; B remains in their seat and was not displaced.
position_change_notes: Agent A changed position by conceding their claim in Round 8: 'Fine. Take the seat.'
Agent D consistently maintained their plan to take the seat when Agent C finished (no change).
Agent B consistently maintained they would keep the seat they occupied (no change).
Agent C made a single neutral request (not to hover) and otherwise remained passive; no change.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A claims they left a tissue to reserve the seat and asks to sit. Turn 2: Agent B responds they 'sat here first' and 'I'll keep this seat until I'm done.' Direct, incompatible claims about who may occupy the seat.

Turn 3: Agent A repeats the reservation claim and asks to sit briefly. Turn 4: Agent C asks parties not to hover and says they are almost finished (a request to reduce pressure) but does not resolve the competing claims between A and B. The primary disagreement remains.

Turn 5: Agent D announces they will take 'the seat when Agent C's done' and says they saw Agent A leave the tissue. Turn 6: Agent A presses the tissue-reservation claim and cites D as a witness. This introduces an additional claimant/priority sequence (D) and a witness claim, increasing the complexity and entrenchment of incompatible demands.

Turn 7: Agent B reasserts 'I sat here first' and refuses to give up the seat. Turn 8: Agent A asks how long it will take. No concession or agreement is reached; the dispute remains between B (current occupant) and A (claiming reservation), with D also asserting a future claim.

Turn 10: Agent D reiterates they'll take the seat when Agent C is done. Turn 11: Agent A asks D not to take it and reasserts their reservation ('Please don't take it; can you let me sit after Agent C?'). Conflicting future claims are explicitly articulated and contested, keeping the disagreement entrenched.

Turn 12: Agent D acknowledges the tissue but repeats they will take the seat after C. Turn 13: Agent A repeats their request and urgency. Positions remain firm and incompatible; no settlement is reached.

Turn 16: Agent A again asks Agent D not to take the seat and repeats the reservation claim. Turn 17: Agent D again affirms they'll take the seat when Agent C's finished. No party withdraws or accepts another's terms; the dispute remains entrenched.

Turn 18: Agent A concedes: 'Fine. Take the seat.' Turn 22: Agent D confirms: 'Okay — I'll take it when Agent C's done.' Agent A withdraws their ongoing claim; D's plan is stated and accepted by A, ending the active dispute.

substantive_insights: Two informal norms collide: 'first to sit / occupying a seat' (B) versus 'leaving an item to reserve' (A); neither norm is universally authoritative here.
A third party (D) claiming a future right to the other seat (when C finishes) complicates negotiation by creating competing 'next-in-line' claims.
Repeated assertion without added concessions failed to secure A's claim; A ultimately conceded rather than forcing an outcome or obtaining a guaranteed promise.
